finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The adverbial condition is duplicated: «متى كانت ... متى كان», and the second verb also disagrees with the plural derivation sequence. The MSA and English do not contain this duplication.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The shared token !!{undischarged} expands to the abstract noun «عدم إسقاط». Repeated constructions such as «الافتراضات مع عدم إسقاطها Γ» force an abstract process noun into an adjectival slot and leave Γ syntactically loose. Meaning is inferable but the recurring grammatical realization is not idiomatic or stable.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: At each occurrence realize the full phrase directly as «الافتراضات غير المسقطة» or «الافتراضات التي لم تُسقط»; retain «عدم الإسقاط» only where an abstract noun is actually required. Record the token-level exception.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Realize each occurrence as a complete phrase headed by «الافتراضات غير المسقطة», recasting sentences so Gamma and Delta are explicit sets of those assumptions; leave the shared noun token unchanged.
finding_dispositions.rationale: The shared token denotes the abstract process «عدم الإسقاط» and cannot grammatically fill these adjectival slots. Sentence-level recasting avoids a loose symbolic apposition.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Medium lexical uncertainty: «الافتراضات التي لم تُسقط» and «الافتراضات المفتوحة» remain plausible alternatives.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Which Arabic proof-theory term best distinguishes an undischarged assumption from a merely open assumption, and should the token system expose separate noun and adjective realizations?

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The induction proves the base case n=0, then states the successor step only for n>0. That omits the transition Γ₀→Γ₁, so the written induction does not establish the claim for all n.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Change «وإن كان~$n>0$» to «ولكل~$n\geq0$، إذا كان~$\Gamma_n\Proves/!A$...» (or induct on n+1 explicitly), then retain the contrapositive argument.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: State the successor step for every n>=0, assuming Gamma_n does not prove A and proving the same for Gamma_{n+1}.
finding_dispositions.rationale: This includes the missing transition Gamma_0 to Gamma_1 without changing the contrapositive argument.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low mathematical uncertainty; the defect is identical in the pinned English source.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Check that the induction is ordinary induction on n with base n=0 and successor step n to n+1 for every n>=0.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The proof says the number of earlier eligible disjunctions decreases at every stage. That is not true: extending Γₙ can make a previously underivable earlier disjunction newly derivable and hence newly eligible. The desired fairness conclusion is true, but the stated monotone-count argument does not prove it.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Fix j once it is eligible. While j remains eligible, every selected i(m) is ≤j; after selection that index is permanently ineligible because a disjunct is added. Only finitely many indices ≤j exist, so j is selected after finitely many further stages.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Fix an eligible index j and use finite fairness: while j remains eligible, each selected i(m) is at most j and becomes permanently ineligible after selection.
finding_dispositions.rationale: Only finitely many indices are at most j, so j must be selected; this replaces the false monotone-count claim.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low mathematical uncertainty; monotonicity of derivability under the increasing Gamma_m construction is the only implicit standard fact.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Verify that eligibility of j persists until selection and that choosing i permanently destroys eligibility of that same index.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: An interpretation of P is constrained only on immediate parent/child pairs that both belong to P, but the next paragraph infers Rf(σ)f(σ.*) for an arbitrary longer extension. For an arbitrary set of prefixed formulas P need not contain the intervening prefixes, so the inference and the closure proposition can fail under the stated definition.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Define an interpretation by requiring Rf(σ)f(τ) whenever σ is a prefix of τ and both lie in P. Alternatively require P to be predecessor-closed and prove that invariant everywhere it is used; the first repair is local and matches the stated arbitrary-Γ scope.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Require Rf(sigma)f(tau) for every pair in P with tau equal to sigma or a finite extension of sigma; update the fresh-prefix extension proof using transitivity.
finding_dispositions.rationale: The definition now supports arbitrary P directly. The f-prime proof shows that every old prefix of sigma.n relates through sigma to the new world.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Medium design uncertainty: predecessor-closure of P would be an alternative global invariant, but it is not part of the stated arbitrary-P definition.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Confirm that all later uses of sigma.* carry the domain condition and that the f-prime construction satisfies the full prefix condition, not only the immediate edge.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The proof cites finitecardisoequal to infer that the predecessor β of an infinite successor ordinal α=β+1 is infinite. That proposition only says distinct finite ordinals are not equinumerous; it does not supply this predecessor-closure inference.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Argue directly: if β∈ω, then β+1∈ω by closure of the natural numbers under successor, contradicting that α is infinite. Hence β is infinite; then invoke ordinfinitycharacter.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: If beta were in omega, closure of omega under successor would put beta+1 in omega, contradicting that alpha is infinite; then apply ordinfinitycharacter.
finding_dispositions.rationale: This removes the citation that did not entail predecessor infinitude and supplies the missing direct argument.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low mathematical uncertainty; the pinned English source retains the same invalid citation.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Check that the edition identifies finite ordinals with members of omega at this point and that ordinfinitycharacter has exactly the now-established hypothesis.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The Classical proof says «كل f:α→β» induces the product map and that this suffices. An arbitrary function does not witness equinumerosity of the products; the hypothesis supplies a bijection, and bijectivity of the induced map must be used.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Write «خذ تقابلًا~$f\colon\alpha\to\beta$ يشهد~$\cardeq{\alpha}{\beta}$؛ فتكون الخريطة ... تقابلًا».
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Choose a bijection f witnessing the hypothesis and state that the coordinatewise product map is again a bijection.
finding_dispositions.rationale: An arbitrary function does not witness product equinumerosity; the proof must use bijectivity.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low mathematical uncertainty. The wording «يشهد الفرض» preserves the protected formula inventory while making the witness role explicit.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Confirm that the coordinatewise product of the chosen bijection and its inverse proves both injectivity and surjectivity.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: Transfinite recursion is rendered as «عملية الاستدعاء ما فوق المتناهي». «استدعاء» denotes calling/invocation, not mathematical recursion, and conflicts with the established «العودية المتناهية التجاوز» used in OLP-0560 and in the MSA.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Replace «عملية الاستدعاء ما فوق المتناهي» with «العودية المتناهية التجاوز» and standardize the neighboring induction/recursion family deliberately.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Use «الاستقراء المتناهي التجاوز» for transfinite induction and «العودية المتناهية التجاوز» for transfinite recursion.
finding_dispositions.rationale: The live, review-bound MSA bytes contain the same mistranslation as Classical, despite the audit comparison note saying otherwise; both layers now match the established OLP-0560 family.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Medium terminology uncertainty: some references prefer «ما فوق المتناهي», but «الاستدعاء» is not mathematical recursion.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Should the edition consistently prefer the adjective «المتناهي التجاوز» over «ما فوق المتناهي» for both induction and recursion?

finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Use «فإن لم توجد قيمة تحقق~$\phi$، فلتكن المجموعة~$\emptyset$.»
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: State the Tarski-Scott empty case once in the same parenthetical order as MSA.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The Hartogs relation reuses α both for the fixed ordinal dom(f)=α and as a set-builder bound variable: f(α) is therefore outside the domain of f. The second variable β is likewise insufficiently bounded. As written R is not a well-defined relation on ran(f).
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Rename the bound variables and bind both below the fixed ordinal: «$R=\Setabs{\tuple{f(\gamma),f(\delta)}\in A\times A}{\gamma,\delta\in\alpha\land\gamma\in\delta}$».
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Use fresh binders gamma and delta, bind both below the fixed ordinal alpha, and transport membership through f.
finding_dispositions.rationale: This eliminates capture of the fixed alpha and ensures both f-applications lie in the domain of f. Using A x A as the ambient product follows the audit; the resulting pairs in fact lie in B x B.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low mathematical uncertainty. B x B would be an equivalent, tighter ambient product.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Verify that both binders are explicitly below alpha and that R is the transported strict well-order on ran(f), with no free or captured beta-like variable.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The added Hausdorff repair applies a free group F of rotations of R³ to «\onesphere», but \onesphere was defined earlier in this same file as the unit circle in R². The inserted set D and every subsequent complement/orbit expression therefore use the wrong carrier.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Introduce a fresh symbol, for example «$S^2=\Setabs{x\in\Real^3}{\lVert x\rVert=1}$», before the Hausdorff paragraph, and replace \onesphere by $S^2$ throughout lines 194–212. Keep the earlier \onesphere for the two-dimensional Vitali argument.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Introduce S^2 as the unit sphere in R^3 and replace only the Hausdorff-passage uses of the earlier R^2 circle symbol.
finding_dispositions.rationale: The live, review-bound MSA bytes share the carrier mismatch. Earlier occurrences of onesphere remain the two-dimensional unit circle for the Vitali construction.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Low notation uncertainty: a different fresh symbol could be used, but the dimension must remain explicit.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Check that every Hausdorff orbit, fixed-point, complement, and absorption expression has carrier S^2 in R^3 while all earlier Vitali expressions retain onesphere in R^2.

finding_dispositions.audit_issue: The absorption step simply says to choose a rotation σ whose iterates σⁿ[D] are pairwise disjoint. That existence is essential to σ[D*]=D*\D but is neither proved nor cited; countability of D is also left unstated.
finding_dispositions.audit_proposed_minimal_repair: Add a short lemma: F is countable and every nonidentity rotation fixes only two sphere points, hence D is countable; choose an axis avoiding D and an angle outside the countable set of angles causing σ^k(d)=d′ for d,d′∈D and k>0. Then the iterates are pairwise disjoint and the displayed absorption identity follows.
finding_dispositions.chosen_repair: Prove D countable, choose an axis avoiding D, exclude the countable union of angles causing a positive iterate to send one D-point to another, and define the resulting two-piece absorption bijection.
finding_dispositions.rationale: For a two-generated free group, D is a countable union of two-point fixed sets. Outside the countable bad-angle set, the sigma^n[D] are pairwise disjoint and sigma[D*]=D* minus D.
finding_dispositions.uncertainty: Medium proof-detail uncertainty: the finite bad-angle count for fixed d,d-prime,k is geometrically standard but remains prose rather than a separately labeled lemma.
finding_dispositions.double_check_prompt: Double-check the fixed-axis bad-angle count, pairwise-disjoint-iterate implication, and that the piecewise rotation/identity map is a bijection S^2 to S^2 minus D compatible with the finite paradoxical partition.
